# AI Migrations

> Lessons from products migrated to another language or framework with AI, for anyone running a
> large project with AI agents.

**Unofficial. No company named here endorses or is affiliated with this project.** Company and
product names describe the subject of each case only. Summaries are in our own words and link to
their primary sources.

<!-- disclosure: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 16 of the 24 cases used Claude models or Claude Code (Bloomberg, Ping.gg, GitHub, Checkly, Intel, Bun, GitLab, Mindstone, Datadog, Lutz Leonhardt, PagerDuty, Ladybird, Christopher Chedeau, Spotify, Robert Marshall, Slack; 6 others leave the models unstated), and Anthropic owns Bun, the subject of one case. GitHub, Intel, Mindstone and Ping.gg also used other vendors' models; where a source compares outcomes by model, that is its author's own unaudited report, and no lesson ranks vendors.

## What it does

<!-- contents: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Now: 24 cases (Slack, Zalando, Airbnb, Google, Robert Marshall, Spotify, Christopher Chedeau, Ladybird, Uber, PagerDuty, Lutz Leonhardt, 1Password, Datadog, Mindstone, GitLab, Bun, Asana, Intel, Checkly, Temporal, Shopify, GitHub, Ping.gg, Bloomberg), 153 lessons on 16 aspect pages, and a checklist of 12 questions.
<!-- /contents -->

- **Cases** ([cases/](cases/)): one file per migration done with AI, from engineering posts,
  papers and official repositories. Each says what AI did, what rule-based tools and people did,
  how the result was checked, the numbers with their basis, and what went wrong, including what
  the source leaves out.
- **Lessons** ([lessons/](lessons/)): what the cases teach about large AI-driven work, by aspect
  (reviews, tests, orchestration, rollout, cost). The sources stay migrations; the lessons apply
  more widely.
- **Checklist** ([checklist.md](checklist.md)): questions a coding agent can measure on a
  repository before a migration, each with a check and the evidence behind it.
- **Pitfalls** ([pitfalls.md](pitfalls.md)): what the old stack does without being asked, by kind
  of move, and seams for moving in steps.
- **For agents** ([llms.txt](llms.txt)): how to use the collection and one line per lesson page;
  it points to the case index for choosing cases, so an agent reads only what it needs.

[index.md](index.md) lists everything. [log.md](log.md) records what each update covered.

## Try it

**No warranty.** Everything here is provided as is, without warranty, under [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) (scripts, MIT) and [`LICENSE-CONTENT.md`](LICENSE-CONTENT.md) (text, CC BY 4.0); the maintainer is not liable for what applying it changes. Read each proposal before you apply it, on a branch or with a backup; a threshold marked "ours" is the maintainer's own starting point, not a measured value.

Open your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) in your project and pick one of two routes:

- [Planning a migration](#planning-a-migration): run the checklist on the project you are
  thinking of moving to another language, framework or major version.
- [Learning from the lessons](#learning-from-the-lessons): compare how AI agents work in any large
  project with what these migrations taught. Lessons tagged "Old system as oracle: no" are the
  place to start; each is still judged by its own words.

The checklist and the lessons guide your agent through what the cases show; they do not decide
for your project. Step 1 is one prompt per route, for the first review and for every revisit: the
agent looks for the route's record in your project (`docs/migration-review.md` or
`docs/ai-lessons-review.md`). With none, it runs the first review; with one, it revisits: it reads
[corrections.md](corrections.md) first (what we published wrong, and how to repair it), then only
what is new in the collection or due in your project, and stops when nothing is. It says in one
line which it did and why. Step 1 only reads your project and changes nothing: you get numbered
findings, each with options and their trade-offs (the agent may say which one the measurements
favour, labelled as its reading), and you choose for each: do an option, later, or skip. Run step
1 in a fresh session and paste step 2 in that same session; steps 2 to 4 are optional. Run step 1 again in a fresh session
when the collection has grown (llms.txt names a newer log entry than your record) or after a few
weeks of work.

### Planning a migration

<a id="step-3-revisit-later"></a>

#### Step 1: review

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow it to review this project for a migration. Change nothing until I choose.
```

Before applying anything, check step 1's claims: a proposal can rest on a wrong reading of your
project.

#### Step 2: apply

Once you have chosen, paste one of these in the same session, with your choices:

```text
Apply what you recommended.
```

```text
Apply 1A and 3B; 2 and 4 later; skip 5.
```

```text
Apply none; write the record.
```

The agent follows the checklist's "How to run" step 9: it writes the record
`docs/migration-review.md` with each chosen proposal's baseline, then applies one proposal at a
time on a branch, stops at the first failing check and reports it.

#### Step 3: revisit

Run step 1 again in a fresh session. Because the record exists, it does the revisit. An older
revisit prompt that starts "Read docs/migration-review.md" still works.

#### Step 4: share what you learned (optional)

A [field report](docs/field-reports.md) says which questions foresaw the problems you hit and
which missed them; it is how the checklist improves. Wait until an item has met its problem since
its baseline (proven, or stopped holding); until then the record says nothing has happened yet.
Nothing is posted until you say yes. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md and follow it. Draft a field report from docs/migration-review.md, scrub it, and show me the exact text before posting. If no item has met its problem since its baseline, write that in the record with the date and do not draft a field report yet.
```

### Learning from the lessons

<a id="step-3-revisit-later-1"></a>

#### Step 1: compare

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow it to compare this project's AI-driven work with the lessons. Change nothing until I choose.
```

Before applying anything, check step 1's claims: a proposal can rest on a wrong reading of your
project.

#### Step 2: apply

Once you have chosen, paste one of these in the same session, with your choices:

```text
Apply what you recommended.
```

```text
Apply 1A and 3B; 2 and 4 later; skip 5.
```

```text
Apply none; write the record.
```

The agent follows step 6 of [applying the lessons](docs/applying-lessons.md): it writes the record
`docs/ai-lessons-review.md` with each chosen proposal's baseline, then applies one proposal at a
time on a branch, stops at the first failing check and reports it.

#### Step 3: revisit

Run step 1 again in a fresh session. Because the record exists, it does the revisit. An older
revisit prompt that starts "Read docs/ai-lessons-review.md" still works.

#### Step 4: share what you learned (optional)

A field report from this route says which lessons held in a project that is not a migration; it
tells us which lessons and "Old system as oracle" tags to re-check against their cases. Wait until
an item has met its problem since its baseline. Nothing is posted until you say yes. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md and follow it. Draft a field report from docs/ai-lessons-review.md, naming which lessons held and which did not, scrub it, and show me the exact text before posting. If no item has met its problem since its baseline, write that in the record with the date and do not draft a field report yet.
```

## Contributing

Corrections are welcome: a wrong number, a broken link, a summary that misreads its source. Open
an issue; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) gives the scope, the
commands and the writing rules, and points to the case format and the other rules in `docs/`.
